title: Playing and recording with Fat Man Williams
summary: Worked with Dave 'Fat Man' Williams at the Lamplighter and downtown, and recorded at Williams's house on a Sunday without knowing the numbers.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Yeah, well we'll start thinking about it, you know, go back to the beginning and think some more and different things. Like the Lamplighter, wasn't that the name of the place you worked with?

Yeah, the horn you asked was the Lamplighter. It was on Bourbon and right across the street from where Pete Barney used to have, before he's had his club, I worked there with Dave, man, Williams, Fat Man Williams. Yeah, that's St. Anne and Bourbon. St. Anne and Bourbon. I worked there with him and somebody else I worked with Dave. Oh, at the downtown, I worked at the downtown with Dave. And quite a few jobs, other outside jobs with Dave. I made the recordings with Dave. I just can't think of everything.
Yeah, well that day at downtown, that's the one at Toulouse and Bourbon or? Toulouse and Bourbon.
How did you make those records? I never did understand that. Right.

We made those with him. As long as I was living back on the lakefront, up on Joe something, we went to his house and recorded those records. Right. His house one Sunday. And the best part about it, I didn't even know what none of us knew what Dave was going to record. None of us knew the numbers. So, this by, by our best by having a pretty good deal, we caught on to the right. Wasn't a trouble at all. But I didn't know none of the numbers because I had never worked rehearsals with, you know. Just quick set up, record those records.
Was that your first job with Dave or?
No, I hadn't been working with Dave. Yeah, I see. All at once he wanted to record his records. That was his own numbers he wanted to record. So, I went on back there and we made them.
Well, they're pretty standard New Orleans numbers. The changes are pretty much the same.
Well, some of them were his own ideas. Really good.
Yeah, but I was trying to imagine some of them. Same old changes like the Bucket changes, but different melodies.
That's right. It seems to me.
